question:
Last week, did you work full-time, part-time, or did you not work at all?
Yes, full-time / Yes, part-time / No

flags.why: The stem offers three choices but the options are yes/no. "No" could mean not full-time, not part-time, or did not work, so it answers the stem unclearly.

flags.quote: did you not work at all?
flags.why: The negative clause makes "No" confusing: it can read as "No, I did not not work", meaning I did work.
"Work" is not defined. Respondents may differ on unpaid family work, own business, one hour of work, or a job they were away from.
It is unclear whether this means the calendar week just ended or the past 7 days. The brief says the past week, with no dates given.
No hours threshold is given, so people with the same hours may choose differently. Someone with two jobs, or hours that varied, has no clear answer.
One "No" covers people on leave, unemployed and looking for work, and not in the labour force. Employment status may need those separated; the analyst should confirm.

items.rewrite: Think about the 7 days from [start date] to [end date]. Paid work means any work for pay or profit, in a job or your own business, even for one hour. Count a job you were away from during that time. How much paid work did you do in those 7 days? Full-time paid work / Part-time paid work / No paid work
